mapCaption: A teaching map. Each box fails on its own. SIP up does not prove the adapter, the location, or the bot.

glossary.meaning: The VCC tenant. Skills, users, lists, and campaigns stay inside it.
Agents or supervisors who can take a campaign's work. A user and a campaign can have more than one.
The permission template for a person. Not a campaign profile.
Overrides defaults such as ANI. One profile is assigned to a campaign. The same profile can be reused.
Inbound, outbound, or autodial. Blended is staffing language, not a fourth type.
The number an inbound campaign answers. A stopped campaign does not answer.
The outcome code on a call. Final disposition stops the other numbers on that record for the campaign.
The default list walk: first number on every record, then the next number.
Finishes the numbers on one record before moving on. Community notes say the compass wording is easy to misread.
The agent sees CRM history before the dial.
The outbound page describes one customer call per available agent. The dialer page also says adaptive pace. Quote the page you mean.
A configured number of calls per agent, with an abandon throttle.
Algorithmic pacing. Product guidance talks about teams larger than about ten agents.
No automatic dial. TCPA manual touch adds typing, blocks paste, and enables Dial on a match.
A campaign field with a warning if you change it. This lab does not state a numeric default.
A named block in the IVR Administrator's Guide, such as Menu, Play, If/Else, or Skill Transfer.
Sends the call toward one or more skills. No skill selected means the Default queue in the community write-up.
Where a Skill Transfer with no skill goes, per the community article.
Reportable only after the edit permission and the reporting flag. Not historical.
Required, with a reporting permission, before standard reports appear.
A report with filters. A July 2026 community article describes about 60 days unless retention is extended.
One of the API names on the APIs and SDKs page.
The path for a CRM that is not a named Plus adapter.
Opens a URL. Not the same object as a Plus adapter.
The listed CRM integrations, using HTTPS and Secure WebSocket.
The default codec in the technical requirements, described as uncompressed.
The preferred lookup for SIP targets in the technical requirements.
The required TLS version. TLS 1.1 is not supported.
Layer-3 handoff, full duplex, BGP failover, in the technical requirements.
Five9's STIR/SHAKEN program. Not the same thing as a local ANI on a profile.
Direct 911 with a dispatchable location. The data sheet names RedSky.
The place responders can find the caller. A stale HQ address fails that test.
Org-admin history: time, user, number, location, recording, SIP invite.
Workforce, quality, analytics, surveys, and recording. Native suite and a Verint partnership are both on the product page.
Knowledge and prompts for Five9 AI apps. This lab does not name a default model.
The key copied from a ChatBot task into VCC for a digital IVA.
The single agent screen. Same underlying technology as the prebuilt CRM adapters, per the desktop page.
Separate clocks for audio, E911 recordings, agent data, campaign state, domains, and DIDs.
The SIP specification. It does not choose your dial plan.
Telephone events, the usual way DTMF rides in the media.

integrations.how: Named in the technical requirements, with Lightning CTI. Package 2.46 is a dated PDF figure.
A script module, including SFDC Einstein. Different from the desktop adapter.
Service Operations and Configurable workspaces. Release names in the PDF this lab read: Australia, Zurich, Yokohama.
Each is a named Plus adapter. This lab does not copy a package number for them.
Bring-your-own CRM when no named adapter exists.
Named prebuilt connections. A local UC client is also about 320 kbps.
Named on the WEM page as a partnership. Not a synonym for native WEM.
Emergency-location partner on the E911 data sheet. Not the ITSP.
One of three SIP stories. The others are your ITSP to Five9 SBCs, or a gateway.
Gateway-to-gateway over internet, VPN, or Direct Connect. Not a UCCX importer.
A ChatBot task key from the matching regional Studio portal into VCC.
Prompts and knowledge. Agent Assist summaries are the initial consumer the page names.
Two different API names. A wallboard and a standard report are different pipes.
STIR/SHAKEN attestation for FCC and CRTC. Separate from profile ANI.

uncertain: Progressive pacing is worded differently on the dialer page and the outbound page. The glossary says so.
Salesforce package 2.46 and the ServiceNow release names are from the technical requirements read in October 2026.
The call-log window of about 60 days is from a community article dated 14 July 2026.
SOAP versus REST is not assigned per API family.
